{{< include _dmai-macros.txt >}}

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless, or lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the
# size. The PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken
# installation whose system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("dmai", quietly = TRUE)) library(dmai) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```

# Abstract

`dmai_app()` opens an application in the web browser that computes monetary aggregates without code: the data and
its columns, one index with its weights and user costs, every method side by side, the user costs and the Divisia
second moments. This vignette describes its pages and how it keeps its results reproducible.

# Starting the application

```{r launch, eval = FALSE}
dmai_app(
    launch.browser = TRUE
  )
```

The application needs the suggested packages **shiny**, **bslib** and **DT**. **magick** with WebP support is
optional: with it the plots are sent to the browser as WebP images, smaller than the same PNG.

# The pages

| Page | What it does |
|---|---|
| Home | what the application does and the order of the pages |
| Data | the simulated example `money_sim` or a CSV file with one row per date; the date, quantity and rate columns (in the same order), the benchmark rate (a column, or the largest component rate) and whether the rates are in percent |
| Index | one method (Divisia, Divisia with simple growth, Fisher, simple sum, currency equivalent), the value at the first date and the logarithm of the growth; interpretation, plot, table, printed output and R code |
| Compare | the chosen methods side by side, as indexes or growth rates |
| User costs | the user cost and weight of every component over time |
| Second moments | the Divisia variance of the growth of the components |
| References | the articles behind the methods, as `dmai_cite()` prints them |

Every result page has the same tabs:

* **Interpretation** gives the plain-language reading of `dmai_interpret()`, with a button that copies it.
* **Plot** shows the figure, which can be saved as PNG, PDF or WebP.
* **Table** shows the numbers, rounded, in a sortable table with buttons to copy them or save them as CSV or Excel.
* **Output** shows the printed result as text, with a button that copies it.

The index page has a further tab, **R code**, with the code that reproduces the result outside the application.

The index page after the Divisia aggregate of `money_sim` with the bond yield `rb` as benchmark:

```{r shot-index, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-index.jpg" else "figures/app-index.webp")
```

its plot, the aggregate against the simple sum:

```{r shot-plot, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-plot.jpg" else "figures/app-plot.webp")
```

the comparison of the methods:

```{r shot-compare, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-compare.jpg" else "figures/app-compare.webp")
```

and the weights of the components:

```{r shot-usercost, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(path = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "figures/app-usercost.jpg" else "figures/app-usercost.webp")
```

# Reproducibility

For the settings of the screenshots, the R code tab shows:

```{r code}
settings <-
  list(
      source  = "example"
    , method  = "Barnett"
    , logbase = "e"
    , date    = "Date"
    , x       = paste0("x", 1:8)
    , r       = paste0("r", 1:8)
    , bench   = "rb"
    , percent = TRUE
    , base    = 100
    )
cat(dmai:::.dmai_app_code(input = settings))
```

The indexes are deterministic, so the code returns the same numbers as the application.

# Deploying

`dmai_app_object()` returns the application object without running it, for a server:

```{r deploy, eval = FALSE}
# app.R on a Shiny server
dmai::dmai_app_object()
```

# References

Barnett, W. A. (1980). Economic monetary aggregates: an application of index number and aggregation theory.
*Journal of Econometrics*, 14(1), 11--48.
